profile.legal_name: Legend Homes by Camillo (founded 1991 as Legend Classic Homes; exact legal entity name not confirmed in a public record this run)
profile.parent: Camillo Companies (family-owned parent brand formed in 2022; Camillo family, Houston)
profile.org_note: Legend Homes is the for-sale homebuilding company (the 'Retail' entity, with the Princeton Classic Homes brand) inside family-owned Camillo Companies, alongside SimplyHome (build-to-rent owner and operator, formerly Camillo Properties), Academy Development (land acquisition and lot development for both) and LCI Services (maintenance). Group CEO Dan Miller sits over a Legend president (Lee Darnold) with three division presidents (Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio) created in early 2026. Land decisions sit outside the builder, at Academy Development under president Sean Mulroony; finance sits at group level with CFO Jomar Ereso and Chief Investment Officer Dror Goldberg. The founder's daughters, Lara Camillo Moynihan and Lauren Camillo Sullivan, are the board members the company lists.
profile.summary: Texas-only entry-level builder (Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio), more than 22,000 homes sold since 1991, and one arm of the Camillo family's vertically integrated group. It is a conventional for-sale builder, but it shares its land pipeline with the build-to-rent affiliate SimplyHome (more than 10,800 rental homes built), and some communities are split between the two. A search-result snippet of Builder's firm profile (page not opened, so unconfirmed) shows 1,457 closings in 2025, down from 2,049 in 2024, with 165 single-family build-to-rent units, so a small part of reported volume may be rentals built for the affiliate. Lots come mainly from affiliate Academy Development, and the group describes itself as one of the largest private landowners in Texas, so this is a land-heavy, self-developing builder rather than a land-light one; a plausible land-banking customer only if the new, finance-led management (CEO from August 2025, CFO from April 2026) chooses to take land off the family balance sheet.
